summary: Agricola is a tense worker-placement farming game where taking an action denies it to everyone else that round, forcing constant recalculation as you build fields, pastures, and a house while keeping your family fed. The harvest phases are the crunch point where under-preparation gets brutally punished.
praised: huge variety from occupation and minor improvement cards
strong sense of building a coherent, self-sufficient farm
criticised: harsh food-penalty scoring feels punishing to newcomers
card-heavy deck can be swingy or push toward solitaire optimization

interaction.kind: worker placement blocking, mostly parallel farm boards
interaction.detail: Players compete for the same limited action spaces each round, so claiming one denies it to everyone else that turn, but each player otherwise develops their own farm tableau independently. Conflict is entirely about racing for shared spaces, not attacking another player's board.

scoring.why: Final score sums fields, pastures, every crop and animal type, house/family size, played improvement/occupation cards, unused spaces, and begging penalties.
scoring.how_you_win: Over 14 rounds you use worker placement to expand your house, plow fields, fence pastures, grow crops and animals, and play cards while feeding your family at each harvest; whoever's farm tallies the highest score across all these categories wins.
